### Configuring setup lifecycle hooks in package.json for Bun templates

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/templating/create.mdx

Configures preinstall, postinstall, and start scripts within the `bun-create` configuration block. Bun strips this section after scaffolding.

```json
{
  "name": "@bun-examples/simplereact",
  "version": "0.0.1",
  "main": "index.js",
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^17.0.2",
    "react-dom": "^17.0.2"
  },
  "bun-create": {
    "preinstall": "echo 'Installing...'", // a single command
    "postinstall": ["echo 'Done!'"], // an array of commands
    "start": "bun run echo 'Hello world!'"
  }
}
```

### Define a start script in package.json

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/quickstart.mdx

Add a start script entry to package.json to execute files with Bun.

```json
{
  "name": "my-app",
  "module": "index.ts",
  "type": "module",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": { // [!code ++]
    "start": "bun run index.ts" // [!code ++]
  }, // [!code ++]
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/bun": "latest"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "typescript": "^7"
  }
}
```

```ts
// For CI environments where user interaction is not possible
await Bun.secrets.set({
  service: "ci-deployment", 
  name: "api-key",
  value: process.env.API_KEY,
  allowUnrestrictedAccess: true // Bypass macOS keychain user prompts
});
```

### Set Up and Run Bun Site Benchmarks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/bench/site/README.md

Sets up required toolchains and dependencies, then runs the full benchmark suite or targeted subsets. Requires Linux x64 and external dependencies like hyperfine, bombardier, and PostgreSQL on PATH.

```sh
bench/site/setup-toolchains.sh                      # node, deno, pnpm/yarn/npm, bun release + canary -> $SITEBENCH_HOME/toolchains
bench/site/setup-repos.sh                           # rolldown/benchmarks clone + deps of bench/express, bench/websocket-server, bench/postgres
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun bench/site/run-all.sh          # everything: bundler http ws postgres install (~30 min with RUNS=3)
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun bench/site/run-all.sh http ws  # a subset
RUNS=1 BUN=... bench/site/run-all.sh                # quick smoke run
```

### Script Profiling

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-inspector-protocol/README.md

Example demonstrating how to start and stop script profiling and handle profiling updates and completion.

```typescript
// Start script profiling with sampling
await inspector.send("ScriptProfiler.startTracking", { includeSamples: true });

// Listen for profiling updates
inspector.on("ScriptProfiler.trackingUpdate", event => {
  console.log("Profiling event:", event);
});

// Stop profiling to get complete data
inspector.on("ScriptProfiler.trackingComplete", data => {
  if (data.samples) {
    // Process stack traces
    console.log(`Collected ${data.samples.stackTraces.length} stack traces`);
  }
});

await inspector.send("ScriptProfiler.stopTracking");
```

### Memory Profiling

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-inspector-protocol/README.md

Example demonstrating how to start and stop heap tracking and listen for garbage collection events.

```typescript
// Start heap tracking
await inspector.send("Heap.enable");
await inspector.send("Heap.startTracking");

// Listen for GC events
inspector.on("Heap.garbageCollected", ({ collection }) => {
  console.log(
    `GC completed: ${collection.type} (${collection.endTime - collection.startTime}ms)`,
  );
});

// ... perform operations to analyze ...

// Get heap snapshot
const { snapshotData } = await inspector.send("Heap.stopTracking");
// Process snapshotData to find memory leaks
```

--------------------------------

### Bun.serve(options)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/http/server.mdx

Configures and starts an HTTP server in Bun. Supports HTTP/3 over QUIC with TLS and customizable idle connection timeouts.

```APIDOC
## Bun.serve(options)

### Description
Starts a Bun HTTP server with support for HTTP/3 over QUIC, TLS configurations, and custom connection idle timeouts.

### Syntax
```ts
Bun.serve(options)
```

### Parameters
- **options** (object) - Configuration object for the HTTP server.
  - **fetch** (Function) - Request handler callback accepting a `req` parameter and returning a `Response`.
  - **http3** (boolean) - Optional. When `true`, enables listening for HTTP/3 over QUIC on UDP. Requires `tls` configuration.
  - **http1** (boolean) - Optional. When set to `false` with `http3: true`, disables TCP listening to serve HTTP/3 only.
  - **tls** (object) - Required if `http3` is enabled. Contains TLS credentials.
    - **key** (BunFile) - Private key file reference.
    - **cert** (BunFile) - Certificate file reference.
  - **idleTimeout** (number) - Optional. Inactivity timeout in seconds before closing connections (default is `10`, maximum is `255`, `0` disables).

### Examples

#### HTTP/3 Server
```ts
Bun.serve({
  tls: {
    key: Bun.file("./key.pem"),
    cert: Bun.file("./cert.pem"),
  },
  http3: true,
  fetch(req) {
    return new Response("Hello over HTTP/3!");
  },
});
```

#### Custom Idle Timeout
```ts
Bun.serve({
  idleTimeout: 30,
  fetch(req) {
    return new Response("Bun!");
  },
});
```
```

```

### Define entrypoint script in TypeScript

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/executables.mdx

### Bun.serve(params)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/http/websockets.mdx

Starts an HTTP and WebSocket server instance using the provided configuration and WebSocket event handlers.

```APIDOC
### Function
`Bun.serve(params: object): Server`

### Parameters
- `params.fetch` (`(req: Request, server: Server) => Response | Promise<Response>`) - Handler for HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrade initiation.
- `params.websocket` (`object`, optional) - WebSocket server configuration and event handlers:
  - `message` (`(ws: ServerWebSocket, message: string | ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array) => void`) - Handler invoked when a message is received.
  - `open` (`(ws: ServerWebSocket) => void`, optional) - Handler invoked when a WebSocket connection is opened.
  - `close` (`(ws: ServerWebSocket, code: number, reason: string) => void`, optional) - Handler invoked when a WebSocket connection is closed.
  - `error` (`(ws: ServerWebSocket, error: Error) => void`, optional) - Handler invoked when an error occurs on a WebSocket.
  - `drain` (`(ws: ServerWebSocket) => void`, optional) - Handler invoked when the socket is ready to accept more data after backpressure.
  - `maxPayloadLength` (`number`, optional) - Maximum message size in bytes (default: `16777216` / 16 MB).
  - `idleTimeout` (`number`, optional) - Connection timeout in seconds (default: `120`).
  - `backpressureLimit` (`number`, optional) - Maximum backpressure in bytes before applying limit behavior (default: `16777216` / 16 MB).
  - `closeOnBackpressureLimit` (`boolean`, optional) - Close socket if backpressure limit is reached (default: `false`).
  - `sendPings` (`boolean`, optional) - Automatically send WebSocket pings (default: `true`).
  - `publishToSelf` (`boolean`, optional) - Receive messages published to subscribed topics by the same socket (default: `false`).
  - `perMessageDeflate` (`boolean | object`, optional) - Compression configuration options.

### Returns
- `Server` - The running server instance.
```

### HTTP/2 GOAWAY Handling with Stream Retries and Non-Replayable Bodies in Node.js

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/web/fetch/H2_TEST_PORT_PLAN.md

This complex example shows how a server sends a GOAWAY frame with a `lastStreamID` that causes some client requests to be retried on a new connection (e.g., GET, POST with Buffer), while others with non-replayable bodies (e.g., POST with ReadableStream) are rejected.

```javascript
let sess = 0; server.on('session', s => { sess++; });
server.on('stream', (stream, h) => {
  if (sess === 1 && stream.id > 1) return; // let goaway kill them
  let body=[]; stream.on('data',c=>body.push(c)); stream.on('end',()=>{}
    stream.respond({':status':200}); stream.end(String(stream.id));
  });
  if (sess === 1 && stream.id === 1) setTimeout(()=>stream.session.goaway(0,1), 30);
});
```

### Bun.serve(options)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/http/routing.mdx

Configures and starts an HTTP server with defined routes and request handlers. Supports asynchronous handlers, parameterized routes, static response objects, and file serving.

```APIDOC
## Bun.serve(options)

### Description
Configures and starts an HTTP server with declarative routing, supporting async/await handlers, route precedence, type-safe path parameters, and zero-allocation static responses.

### Syntax
```ts
Bun.serve(options)
serve(options)
```

### Parameters
- **options** (object) - Configuration options for the HTTP server.
  - **port** (number, optional) - The port number for the server to listen on.
  - **routes** (Record<string, Function | Response>, optional) - A map of URL path patterns to handler functions or static `Response` instances.

### Route Handler Specifications
- **Handler Function**: `(req: BunRequest) => Response | Promise<Response>` - A synchronous or asynchronous function returning a `Response` or `Promise<Response>`.
  - **req.params** (Record<string, string>) - Object containing automatically percent-decoded route parameter values.
- **Static Response**: `Response` - Direct `Response` object cached for zero-allocation dispatch without executing a handler function.

### Route Precedence Rules
Routes match in order of specificity:
1. Exact routes (`/users/all`)
2. Parameter routes (`/users/:id`)
3. Wildcard routes (`/users/*`)
4. Global catch-all (`/*`)

### Examples

#### Async Route Handlers
```ts
import { sql, serve } from "bun";

serve({
  port: 3001,
  routes: {
    "/api/version": async () => {
      const [version] = await sql`SELECT version()`;
      return Response.json(version);
    },
  },
});
```

#### Type-safe Route Parameters
```ts
import type { BunRequest } from "bun";

Bun.serve({
  routes: {
    "/orgs/:orgId/repos/:repoId": (req: BunRequest<"/orgs/:orgId/repos/:repoId">) => {
      const { orgId, repoId } = req.params;
      return Response.json({ orgId, repoId });
    },
  },
});
```

#### Static and File Responses
```ts
Bun.serve({
  routes: {
    "/health": new Response("OK"),
    "/logo.png": new Response(await Bun.file("./logo.png").bytes()),
    "/download.zip": new Response(Bun.file("./download.zip")),
  },
});
```
```

bun install --filter './packages/pkg-a'
```

### bun init <folder?>

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/snippets/cli/init.mdx

Initializes a new Bun project in the specified directory or the current directory with optional templates and preset configurations.

```APIDOC
## bun init <folder?>

### Description
Initializes project files and configuration for the chosen options. Exact files vary by template.

### Usage
```bash
bun init <folder?> [options]
```

### Arguments
- **folder** (string, optional) - Target directory to initialize the project in.

### Options
- **--yes**, **-y** (boolean) - Accept all default prompts without asking questions.
- **--minimal**, **-m** (boolean) - Only initialize type definitions (skip app scaffolding).
- **--react** (string | boolean) - Scaffold a React project. When used without a value, creates a baseline React app. Accepts preset values: `tailwind` (React app preconfigured with Tailwind CSS), `shadcn` (React app with `@shadcn/ui` and Tailwind CSS).
- **--help**, **-h** (boolean) - Print this help menu.

### Examples

**Accept all defaults**
```bash
bun init -y
```

**React**
```bash
bun init --react
```

**React + Tailwind CSS**
```bash
bun init --react=tailwind
```

**React + @shadcn/ui**
```bash
bun init --react=shadcn
```
```

### Bun.serve(options)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/http/routing.mdx

Initializes and runs an HTTP server in Bun with route-based request dispatching and fallback handlers.

```APIDOC
## Bun.serve(options)

### Description
Starts an HTTP server that routes incoming requests using path patterns or falls back to a general `fetch` handler. Route handlers receive a `BunRequest` object and return a standard `Response` or `Promise<Response>`.

### Signature
```ts
Bun.serve(options: {
  routes?: Record<string, (req: BunRequest) => Response | Promise<Response>>;
  fetch?: (req: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>;
})
```

### Parameters
- **options** (object) - Server configuration object.
  - **routes** (Record<string, Function>) - Optional. Key-value mapping of path strings (static paths, parameters, wildcards) to handler functions.
  - **fetch** (Function) - Optional. Handler function invoked when an incoming request does not match any route defined in `routes`.

### Types
#### BunRequest
```ts
interface BunRequest<T extends string = string> extends Request {
  params: Record<T, string>;
  readonly cookies: CookieMap;
}
```

### Example
```ts
Bun.serve({
  routes: {
    "/": () => new Response("Home"),
    "/api": () => Response.json({ success: true }),
    "/users": async () => Response.json({ users: [] }),
  },
  fetch() {
    return new Response("Unmatched route");
  },
});
```
```
